name: Autosomal Dominant Charcot-Marie-Tooth Disease Type 2B

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Genetic Diagnostic Criteria for CMT2B

criteria.description: Presence of distal muscle weakness and atrophy predominantly in lower limbs with sensory loss
Nerve conduction studies showing axonal neuropathy with reduced amplitude of sensory and motor responses
Identification of pathogenic variants in the RAB7A gene
Autosomal dominant inheritance pattern with affected first-degree relatives
Presence of pes cavus or hammer toes

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of clinical neuropathy, supportive electrophysiological findings, and pathogenic RAB7A mutation
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Genetic confirmation is essential for definitive diagnosis due to phenotypic overlap with other CMT subtypes.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Distal muscle atrophy of lower limbs
searchTerms: muscle loss in calves and feet

pathognomonic.symptomName: Sensory loss predominantly affecting distal lower limbs
searchTerms: loss of feeling in lower legs

pathognomonic.symptomName: Ulceromutilating neuropathy with distal ulcerations and infections
pathognomonic.notes: Characteristic ulcerations on feet due to sensory loss
searchTerms: infected wounds on hands or feet

common.symptomName: Distal muscle weakness in upper limbs
Reduced or absent deep tendon reflexes
Distal sensory neuropathy with impaired vibration and proprioception
searchTerms: numbness and tingling in hands and feet
loss of position sense in extremities
burning pain in hands and feet
nerve pain in fingers and toes

occasional.symptomName: Mild foot deformities such as hammer toes

searchTerms: hands and feet feel cold easily
sensitivity to cold in fingers and toes
poor tolerance to cold in limbs
problems with automatic body functions including low blood pressure when standing
autonomic nervous system dysfunction causing dizziness

laboratory: Nerve biopsy showing axonal degeneration with loss of myelinated fibers
imaging: MRI may show muscle atrophy in distal limbs
Ultrasound of peripheral nerves may show reduced cross-sectional area
other: Electrophysiological studies consistent with axonal sensorimotor neuropathy

distinguishingFeatures: Demyelinating neuropathy with slowed nerve conduction velocities
Symmetric distal sensory loss without muscle atrophy early

redFlags: Rapid progression of weakness or sensory loss
Development of foot ulcers with infection
Signs of autonomic dysfunction such as orthostatic hypotension
references: Bird TD. Charcot-Marie-Tooth Neuropathy Type 2B. GeneReviews® [Internet]. 2020.
Pareyson D, Marchesi C. Diagnosis, natural history, and management of Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease. Lancet Neurol. 2009.
